definition_zh: 枯萎；凋谢；使枯萎；逐渐衰退
definition_en: to become dry and shrivel up, or to make something dry and weak
core_image: 一片叶子卷起边缘，颜色从绿褪成干褐
scene: 阳台上的绿植被忘在烈日下，几天后叶子全都垂下来。Left without water, the flowers withered within a week.
sceneCN: 这里 wither 是「枯萎」（第 1 个义项：因缺水而干缩凋谢）；句意：由于没有浇水，那些花在一周之内就枯萎了。

derivatives.zh: wither 加 -ed 构成，意为「枯萎的；干瘪的」
wither 加 -ing 构成，意为「令人难堪的；摧毁性的」
与 wither 同形异源，指马肩隆（两肩之间的隆起）

senses.title: To dry out and shrivel
senses.definition: to become dry, wrinkled and weak, especially through lack of water or through heat
senses.definitionCN: 尤指因缺水或受热而变得干瘪、皱缩、无力
senses.example: The roses withered soon after they were cut.
senses.exampleCN: 玫瑰剪下没多久就枯萎了。
senses.why: The English word appears to come from a Germanic source meaning to shrivel, so the basic sense is the visible drying of a plant.
senses.whyCN: 该词一般被认为源出日耳曼语中表示「干缩」的词，基本义就是植物可见的干枯。

senses.title: To fade away over time
senses.definition: to become weaker, less important or less active over a long period
senses.definitionCN: 在长期中变得弱小、不重要或不再活跃
senses.example: The town withered after the factory closed.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂倒闭后，这个小镇逐渐衰败。
senses.why: A plant that loses water shrinks inward, and the same picture extends to towns, hopes and institutions that slowly lose their strength.
senses.whyCN: 缺水的植物会向内干缩，这一意象被推广到慢慢失去力量的城镇、希望与机构。

senses.title: To make someone feel crushed
senses.definition: to make a person feel foolish, ashamed or small by a cold word or look
senses.definitionCN: 用冷言冷眼使某人觉得愚蠢、羞惭或渺小
senses.example: One withering look from the teacher silenced him.
senses.exampleCN: 老师一个令人生畏的眼神就让他住口了。
senses.why: When a person is dried up by a glance, the bodily shrinking of a plant becomes a picture of confidence collapsing.
senses.whyCN: 人因一瞥而像植物般「被吹干」，于是植物的身形干缩成了自信崩塌的画面。

intro.en: Wither is an English verb, probably from an Old English verb meaning to shrivel, though the exact parent form is uncertain.
intro.cn: wither 是英语动词，一般认为出自古英语中表示「干缩」的动词，但确切的原形存疑。

items.en: A Germanic root links the idea of withering with shrinking and losing strength.
items.cn: 一般认为日耳曼语词根把「凋谢」与「收缩、失去力量」联系在一起。

items.en: A verb for drying up and fading is recorded in Old English texts.
items.cn: 古英语文献中已有表示干枯、凋谢的动词。

items.en: Wither settles into the present spelling and is used for plants and people.
items.cn: 中古英语时期写作 wither，用于植物和人。

items.en: The farming phrase wither on the vine appears in the following centuries.
items.cn: 农事比喻「藤上枯死」在此后几个世纪中出现。

items.en: The verb widens to towns, trade and reputations that fade away.
items.cn: 现代英语中该动词扩展到衰败的城镇、生意与声望。

items.en: The adjective withering also names a crushing comment or glance.
items.cn: 形容词 withering 也指令人难堪的评论或目光。

note.en: Wither is close to within in spelling but unrelated in origin, and close to shrivel and wilt in meaning.
note.cn: wither 在拼写上与 within 相近但词源无关，在意义上与 shrivel、wilt 相近。

entries.definition: inside something
entries.definitionCN: 在……之内；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: dried up and shrunk
entries.definitionCN: 枯萎的；干瘪的

entries.definition: very critical or cutting
entries.definitionCN: 令人难堪的；摧毁性的

entries.definition: to become wrinkled and smaller through heat or loss of water
entries.definitionCN: 因受热或失水而皱缩

entries.definition: to bend and droop from heat or lack of water
entries.definitionCN: 变蔫；下垂

entries.definition: to lose colour or strength slowly
entries.definitionCN: 衰退；褪色

normalIntro.en: Wither is a wetness word: when the water leaves a leaf, the leaf withers, so the sound of the dry word carries the loss of water.
normalIntro.cn: wither 可以和「失去水分」联系在一起：水离开叶子，叶子就枯萎；词音本身也带着一种干涩感。

normal.en: Wither away is the standard phrasal form for fading out gradually.
normal.cn: wither away 是表示逐渐消失的固定短语形式。

normal.en: To wither on the vine means to be wasted before it is used.
normal.cn: wither on the vine 意为在发挥作用之前就被荒废。

normal.en: Withered carries the -ed of the past participle and works as an adjective.
normal.cn: withered 带过去分词词尾 -ed，可作形容词使用。

normal.en: Withers, the horse anatomy word, is a homograph from a different root.
normal.cn: withers 表示马肩隆，与 wither 同形但词源不同。

normal.en: Compare wilt: wilt mostly drops leaves, wither dries and shrivels them.
normal.cn: 对比 wilt：wilt 多指叶子下垂，wither 则指干枯皱缩。

abstract.en: Picture a green leaf curling into a brittle brown cup.
abstract.cn: 想象一片绿叶卷成干褐色的脆杯。

abstract.en: Imagine a forgotten plant on a windowsill, its soil cracked.
abstract.cn: 想象窗台上被遗忘的植物，盆土裂开。

abstract.en: Think of a proud face shrinking after one cold remark.
abstract.cn: 想象一张骄傲的脸在冷言之后委顿下去。

examples.en: Without rain the crops withered in the fields.
examples.cn: 没有雨水，田里的庄稼枯萎了。

examples.en: Hope of a quick deal withered after the meeting.
examples.cn: 会议之后，迅速成交的希望渐渐破灭。

examples.en: She gave him a withering glance and walked away.
examples.cn: 她冷冷地瞥了他一眼，转身走开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂得」——花「喂得」再勤也留不住的水，一干就枯萎；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为源出日耳曼语中表示「干缩、失去水分」的动词，经古英语传入 → 中古英语 wither，核心义「因失水而向内干缩」。

sensesIntro.en: Wither begins with plants drying up, widens to towns and hopes fading over time, and finally describes a person dried up by a cold word or look.
sensesIntro.cn: wither 先指植物干枯，再扩展到城镇与希望随时间衰败，最后指人被冷言冷眼弄得委顿。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a leaf whose edges curl as its colour turns from green to dry brown.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片叶子边缘卷起，颜色从绿褪成干褐。

branches.en: The drying plant is the physical sense.
branches.cn: 植物干枯是字面义项。

branches.en: Slow loss of strength is the figurative sense for places and hopes.
branches.cn: 缓慢失去力量是关于地方与希望的比喻义项。

branches.en: A person shrunk by a cold look gives the social sense.
branches.cn: 人被冷眼弄得萎缩，生出人情层面的义项。

branches.en: Both the plant and the town follow the same slow curve of decline.
branches.cn: 植物衰枯与城镇衰败遵循同一条缓慢下滑的曲线。

branches.en: Confidence and reputation can each be dried out by time or by a word.
branches.cn: 自信与声誉都可能被时间或一句话抽干。

intro.en: Wither is a simple Germanic verb with few affixes, but it yields the adjective forms withered and withering.
intro.cn: wither 是简单的日耳曼语源动词，词缀不多，但能派生出形容词 withered 与 withering。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin ancestor, so there are no Latin cognates to note.
latinIntro.cn: 该词没有拉丁语祖先，因此没有可记录的拉丁同源词。

items.example: Wither is the base verb.
items.exampleCN: wither 是基础动词。

items.meaningCN: 构成过去分词或形容词的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ed forms withered.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 withered。

items.example: Withered leaves lay on the path.
items.exampleCN: 枯叶散落在小路上。

items.meaning: forming a present participle or adjective
items.meaningCN: 构成现在分词或形容词的后缀
items.example: The suffix -ing forms withering.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成 withering。

items.example: Withering describes a harsh remark.
items.exampleCN: withering 形容严厉的说法。

items.meaning: the ridge above a horse shoulders
items.example: Withers is a homograph from another source.
items.exampleCN: withers 是同形异源词。

items.example: Wither away is a common phrasal use.
items.exampleCN: wither away 是常见短语用法。

items.example: Withering away appears in political writing.
items.exampleCN: withering away 常见于政治论述。

definition_zh: 子宫；产生或孕育事物的源头
definition_en: the organ in a woman or female mammal where a baby develops before birth, or a place where something new is formed
core_image: 一个温暖幽暗的圆形房间，生命在这里被孕育成型
scene: 医生指着屏幕上的影像，告诉准妈妈胎儿在她的肚子里成长。The doctor pointed at the scan and explained that the baby was growing safely inside the womb.
sceneCN: 这里 womb 是「子宫」（第 1 个义项：女性或雌性哺乳动物孕育胎儿的器官）；句意：医生指着影像，解释说胎儿正在子宫里安全地成长。

derivatives.zh: 由名词加类比词尾构成，形容像子宫一样温暖、封闭、孕育性的空间
罕见用法，由名词加词尾构成，形容宽敞、幽深、像腔室一样的
由介词与名词构成的复合修饰语，指「胎儿时期的、宫内发生的」

senses.title: The organ that carries an unborn baby
senses.definition: the organ in a woman or female mammal in which a baby grows before birth
senses.definitionCN: 女性或雌性哺乳动物体内孕育胎儿的器官
senses.example: The baby turned head down in the womb during the last month.
senses.exampleCN: 最后一个月里，胎儿在子宫中转为头朝下的姿势。
senses.why: The Old English word meant the belly or the inside of the body, and that inner empty space became the image of the organ that holds new life.
senses.whyCN: 古英语原义是「腹部、体内」，这个「身体内部的空腔」意象自然用来指容纳新生命的器官。

senses.title: A place where something is conceived
senses.definition: a place, time, or situation in which ideas or projects begin to grow
senses.definitionCN: 思想、事业开始萌发成长的地方、时期或情境
senses.example: Those two friends described their little kitchen as the womb of the business idea.
senses.exampleCN: 那两位朋友把自家的小厨房称为这个商业点子的孕育之处。
senses.why: If the body organ is where a life grows, then any warm protected space where a new thing slowly forms can borrow the same picture.
senses.whyCN: 如果子宫是生命成长的地方，那么任何温暖而有保护性、新事物慢慢成形的地方，都能借用这个画面。

senses.title: Life before birth
senses.definition: the period or state of being an unborn baby inside the mother
senses.definitionCN: 作为胎儿待在母亲体内的时期或状态
senses.example: He has been blind since the womb, so the whole world was taught to him by sound.
senses.exampleCN: 他自母胎中就是盲的，所以整个世界都是通过声音教给他的。
senses.why: The organ stands for the time spent inside it, so phrases such as from the womb point to life before birth.
senses.whyCN: 器官可以代指在其中的时间，所以「自子宫起」这类说法指的就是出生之前的那段生活。

senses.title: The dark warm inner space
senses.titleCN: 温暖幽闭的内里；庇护之所
senses.definition: a figurative image of a dark, warm, enclosed and protective inner space
senses.definitionCN: 幽暗、温暖、封闭而有保护感的内部空间的比喻
senses.example: The old library felt like a womb of quiet for the tired students.
senses.exampleCN: 对疲惫的学生来说，那座老图书馆就像一个安静的庇护所。
senses.why: Because a baby inside the organ knows warmth and darkness rather than light, writers use it for any shelter that feels enclosed and safe.
senses.whyCN: 因为胎儿在器官里感受到的是温暖与黑暗而非光线，作家便用它来比喻任何封闭而安全的庇护之处。

intro.en: Womb goes back to Old English wamb or womb, meaning the belly, and the sense of the organ carrying a baby grew from that inner-space image.
intro.cn: womb 源自中古英语的 wamb、womb，再往前是古英语词汇，原义为腹部、体内，后由「体内空腔」发展为容纳胎儿的器官。

items.en: A reconstructed root seen by some scholars as related to the belly or a hollow body part.
items.cn: 一般认为有重构词根与腹部或中空的躯体部位相关，但具体形式存疑。

items.en: A Germanic noun for the belly or the inside of the body.
items.cn: 日耳曼语族中表示腹部或体内部位的词形。

items.en: Wamb and womb name the belly and the inner cavity of the body.
items.cn: 古英语 wamb、womb 指腹部与体内的腔室。

items.en: The word shifts towards the organ in which a baby is carried.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，词义逐渐转向孕育胎儿的器官。

items.en: Womb is now mainly the organ of pregnancy, and also a metaphor for any place of origin.
items.cn: 现代英语中主要指妊娠器官，也用于比喻任何发源之处。

note.en: Womb sits among the anatomy words uterus and belly, the figure-of-speech item cradle, and look-alike words such as comb and tomb.
note.cn: womb 与解剖学上的 uterus、belly，以及比喻类的 cradle，还有 comb、tomb 等形近词相邻。

entries.definition: a grave or a stone building for a dead person
entries.definitionCN: 坟墓：与 womb 拼写相近而词源不同，仅字母顺序像

entries.definition: a tool with teeth for arranging hair
entries.definitionCN: 梳子：与 womb 押韵，拼写与词源都不同

entries.definition: injured by a cut or blow
entries.definitionCN: 受伤的：与 womb 字形近似，来自 wound，词源无关

entries.definition: the medical name for the organ of pregnancy
entries.definitionCN: 子宫的医学正式名称，womb 更日常、更文学

entries.definition: the front part of the body below the chest
entries.definitionCN: 腹部：与 womb 的古义相同，现指整个腹部

entries.definition: a small bed for a baby, or the place where something began
entries.definitionCN: 摇篮，也引申为发源地，与 womb 的比喻义接近

normalIntro.en: Womb rhymes with loom: a dark, quiet room inside the body where a new life is woven.
normalIntro.cn: womb 与 loom 押韵：它就是身体里一间幽暗安静的房间，新生命在里面被织成。

normal.en: The preposition in is the usual partner: the baby grows in the womb.
normal.cn: 最常用的介词是 in：「the baby grows in the womb」。

normal.en: From the womb means from the very beginning of life.
normal.cn: from the womb 表示从生命最开始的时候起。

normal.en: Uterus is the medical term; womb is the common and warmer word.
normal.cn: uterus 是医学术语，womb 是更常见也更温暖的词。

normal.en: The plural is simply wombs, and the word never forms a verb.
normal.cn: 复数直接加 s 变成 wombs，这个词从不作动词用。

normal.en: The same picture gives the phrase the womb of a new age for a birthplace or origin.
normal.cn: 同一幅画面也带来「创生之所」式的说法，如新时代的摇篮或源头。

abstract.en: Think of a round, warm room lit only by a faint red glow.
abstract.cn: 想象一间圆形的温暖房间，只有微弱的红光照明。

abstract.en: Picture a seed curled inside a soft closed shell.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子蜷缩在柔软闭合的壳里。

abstract.en: Hear the w at both ends of the word like two arms folded around a body.
abstract.cn: 留意词首和词尾的两个 w，像两只手臂环抱住一个身体。

examples.en: The scan showed that the twins were lying head to head in the womb.
examples.cn: 检查显示双胞胎在子宫里头碰头地躺着。

examples.en: The small town likes to call itself the womb of the national theatre.
examples.cn: 这个小镇喜欢把自己称作国家剧院的摇篮。

examples.en: Doctors can now treat some diseases before birth, inside the womb.
examples.cn: 如今医生可以在胎儿还在子宫内时就治疗某些疾病。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「温」——子宫就是一个温（womb）暖黑暗的小屋子，与词源无关，只是读音联想。

root: 古英语 wamb、womb（腹部、体内）→ 中古英语 womb（子宫）→ 英语 womb，核心义「身体内部的空腔」。

sensesIntro.en: Womb runs from the real organ, through the time spent inside it, to any warm protected place where something begins.
sensesIntro.cn: womb 从真实的器官出发，经在其中的时间，延伸到任何温暖受保护、新事物开始的地方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a warm, dark, round room where a new life is formed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间温暖幽暗的圆形房间，新生命在其中成形。

branches.en: The organ itself is the everyday anatomical sense.
branches.cn: 器官本身是最日常的解剖义项。

branches.en: A place of origin borrows the picture of a place that nurses new things.
branches.cn: 「发源地」借用了孕育新事物之地的画面。

branches.en: The organ stands for the period spent inside it.
branches.cn: 器官代指在其中度过的那段时期。

branches.en: The metaphor of a dark, warm, enclosed inner space.
branches.cn: 幽暗温暖封闭的内部空间这一比喻。

branches.en: All three share the single image of an enclosed warm space holding life.
branches.cn: 三者共享同一个意象：封闭温暖的空间承载生命。

intro.en: Womb is a single Old English noun with no derivational affix, so the word family grows mainly through compounds such as womb-like and in-womb.
intro.cn: womb 是一个没有派生词缀的古英语名词，词族主要通过 womb-like、in-womb 之类的复合形式扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin has no shared root here; the dictionary word for the organ is uterus or matriz, which entered English separately.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有共同的拉丁词根；拉丁语指子宫的词是 uterus 与 matriz，它们以不同的路径进入英语。

items.example: Womb is one of the oldest body words in English.
items.exampleCN: womb 是英语中最古老的躯体词汇之一。

items.example: The suffix -s gives wombs.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 wombs。

items.meaning: more than one organ of this kind
items.example: Wombs appears in medical texts about several patients.
items.exampleCN: wombs 出现在针对多位患者的医学文本中。

items.example: The suffix -like forms womb-like.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -like 构成 womb-like。

items.example: The cabin had a womb-like warmth.
items.exampleCN: 小木屋有一种子宫般的温暖。

items.example: The prefix in- forms in-womb.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 构成 in-womb。

items.meaning: the medical name for the organ
items.example: Doctors write uterus where a patient would say womb.
items.exampleCN: 医生写 uterus，而病人通常说 womb。

items.example: Maternal is used for the mother side of this field.
items.exampleCN: maternal 用于这一义场中母亲的一面。

items.example: Cradle shares the birth metaphor.
items.exampleCN: cradle 共享「诞生」这一比喻。

definition_zh: 啄木鸟；比喻不停敲击、刨根问底的人
definition_en: a bird with a strong pointed beak that climbs tree trunks and strikes the wood to find insects inside
core_image: 一只鸟用爪勾住树干，尾巴撑住身体，头不停地往木头里敲
scene: 清晨林子里传来急促的敲击声，抬头一看，一只鸟正贴着树干往上爬，用尖嘴凿开树皮找虫子。A rapid drumming came from the woods, and a woodpecker was climbing the trunk, chiseling the bark open for insects.
sceneCN: 这里 woodpecker 是「啄木鸟」（第 1 个义项：用尖喙敲击树木找虫的鸟）；句意：林子里传来急促的敲击声，一只啄木鸟正攀在树干上凿开树皮找虫子。

pos.zh: 啄木鸟；不停敲击或追问的人

collocations.zh: 像啄木鸟一样（不停地敲）
在树干上鼓敲的啄木鸟

derivatives.zh: 由复合名词加动名词词尾构成，指啄木般连续敲击的动作
复合词的第一部分，原义为「树木、林地」
复合词的第二部分，义为「用尖喙啄」，也可单独使用

senses.title: The bird that drums on trunks
senses.definition: a bird with a strong straight beak and stiff tail feathers that clings to trees and drills into the wood for insects
senses.definitionCN: 有坚硬直喙和坚硬尾羽、攀附树上凿木取虫的鸟
senses.example: The woodpecker drilled a neat row of small holes in the dead trunk.
senses.exampleCN: 啄木鸟在枯树干上凿出一排整齐的小洞。
senses.why: The compound simply names the action that defines the bird: it pecks at wood, so it is a wood-pecker.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词直接点明鸟的标志性动作：它啄木头，所以就是「啄木者」。

senses.title: The sharp knocking sound
senses.definition: a quick repeated knocking that sounds like a bird striking a tree
senses.definitionCN: 像鸟击打树木那样短促而重复的敲击声
senses.example: All night the pipes made a woodpecker noise above the ceiling.
senses.exampleCN: 水管整夜在头顶天花板上发出啄木鸟般的敲击声。
senses.why: Because the bird is heard long before it is seen, its name easily moves to the sound it makes.
senses.whyCN: 因为人们往往先听到鸟声、后看到鸟，这个词也就很容易转指它发出的声音。

senses.title: A person who keeps hammering at something
senses.definition: a person who goes on striking or questioning something persistently, like a bird chiseling a hole
senses.definitionCN: 像鸟凿洞那样不停敲打、反复追问的人
senses.example: Our auditor is a real woodpecker and will not stop until every figure is checked.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的审计员真是不折不扣的啄木鸟，不把每个数字都核实就不罢休。
senses.why: The bird drills through solid wood by sheer repetition, so the word lends itself to anyone who drills into problems by force and persistence.
senses.whyCN: 啄木鸟靠反复敲击凿穿实心木头，于是这个词自然用来比喻靠力气和执着钻透问题的人。

senses.title: A family of climbing birds
senses.definition: any member of the bird family whose members climb trees and drill for food or nest holes
senses.definitionCN: 攀树啄木觅食或筑巢的整个鸟类类群
senses.example: The park protects several woodpeckers, including the small spotted kind.
senses.exampleCN: 公园保护着好几种啄木鸟类，包括斑纹的小型种类。
senses.why: Once the name covered one bird, classifiers extended it to the whole family that shares the same striking and climbing habits.
senses.whyCN: 名称先是属于一种鸟，随后分类学家把它扩展到所有拥有同样凿击与攀爬习性的整个科。

intro.en: Woodpecker is a modern English compound, formed from wood and the agent noun pecker, so it literally means the one that pecks wood.
intro.cn: woodpecker 是现代英语复合词，由 wood 与表示施动者的 pecker 组成，字面义为「啄木头的东西」。

items.en: The bird was known by native names such as the tree-specca, literally the tree-specker.
items.cn: 古英语中这种鸟有 treowspic 之类本土名称，字面义为「啄树者」。

items.en: Pechen means to pick at food with the beak, and pecker names the one who does it.
items.cn: 中古英语 pecchen 意为用喙啄食，pecker 指这样做的人或物。

items.en: Wood pecker appears in written English, joining the object wood with the agent pecker.
items.cn: 一般认为十六世纪书面英语出现 wood pecker 的写法，把宾语 wood 与施动词 pecker 合在一起。

items.en: The spelling settles into a single word, woodpecker.
items.cn: 十七世纪前后拼写定形为一个词 woodpecker。

items.en: The word also grows a figurative sense for a persistent knocking or questioning person.
items.cn: 现代英语又发展出比喻义，指不停敲击或追问的人。

note.en: Woodpecker belongs with other pecking compounds such as nuthatch and treecreeper, and with related climbing and drumming birds.
note.cn: woodpecker 与其他「啄食」类复合鸟名如 nuthatch、treecreeper 相邻，也与攀树、鼓鸣的同类鸟相邻。

entries.definition: a bird or person that pecks
entries.definitionCN: 啄食的鸟或人；是 woodpecker 的施动部分

entries.definition: to strike or pick up with the beak
entries.definitionCN: 用喙啄击或啄取；构成复合词的第二部分

entries.definition: a small shrike that hunts from thorny woods
entries.definitionCN: 林间小型伯劳：与 woodpecker 同样以 wood 起首，但属不同鸟科

entries.definition: a small bird that climbs trunks and cracks nuts in bark
entries.definitionCN: 䴓：能攀树干、在树皮里夹开坚果的小鸟，与啄木鸟习性相近

entries.definition: a tiny bird that creeps up trunks looking for insects
entries.definitionCN: 旋木雀：沿树干爬行找虫的小鸟

entries.definition: a North American bird that drills holes to drink tree sap
entries.definitionCN: 吸汁啄木鸟：北美的啄木鸟类，主要钻洞喝树汁

normalIntro.en: Break the shape into wood plus pecker: an animal whose job, in the name, is simply pecking wood.
normalIntro.cn: 把词形拆成 wood 加 pecker：这个名字本身就把鸟的工作写了出来——啄木头。

normal.en: Wood names the material and pecker names the worker, just as in woodcutter.
normal.cn: wood 指材料，pecker 指干活的一方，与 woodcutter 的构词方式一样。

normal.en: The verb peck describes short sharp blows, which is exactly how the bird eats.
normal.cn: 动词 peck 表示短促有力的啄击，正是这种鸟进食的方式。

normal.en: The plural is woodpeckers, and the word stays a noun.
normal.cn: 复数形式是 woodpeckers，这个词始终只作名词。

normal.en: Compare nuthatch and treecreeper, two other birds named for how they move on bark.
normal.cn: 对比 nuthatch 与 treecreeper，这两种鸟也是按它们在树皮上的动作命名的。

normal.en: For the person sense, think of someone who keeps hammering away at one question.
normal.cn: 说到「人」的义项，就想象一个人对同一个问题反复敲打追问。

abstract.en: Watch the bird brace its stiff tail against the bark and hammer upward.
abstract.cn: 想象这只鸟用坚硬的尾羽抵住树皮，一边往上爬一边敲。

abstract.en: Hear the rapid trr-trr-trr of drumming across a quiet morning forest.
abstract.cn: 想象安静的晨林里传来快速连续的笃笃笃声。

abstract.en: Picture a neat round hole where the bird will raise its young.
abstract.cn: 想象一个整齐的圆洞，鸟将在里面抚育雏鸟。

examples.en: A woodpecker works its way up the old oak, tapping as it climbs.
examples.cn: 一只啄木鸟沿着老橡树向上攀，一边爬一边敲。

examples.en: Two woodpeckers have nested in the same hollow for years.
examples.cn: 两只啄木鸟在这个树洞里住了好多年。

examples.en: The drumming of a woodpecker was the only sound in the park.
examples.cn: 啄木鸟的敲击声是公园里唯一的声音。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啄 wood」——把木头啄开的就是啄木鸟；这只是拆读联想，与词源无关。

root: wood（木头）+ peck（啄，中古英语 pecchen）+ -er（施动者）→ woodpecker，字面义「啄木头的东西」。

sensesIntro.en: The name starts with the bird itself, jumps to its knocking sound, and finally serves as a figure for any stubborn hammering or questioning.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名字从鸟本身出发，转到它敲出的声音，最后比喻任何执着的敲打与追问。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bird braced on a trunk, hammering its beak into the bark.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只鸟抵住树干，把喙不停地凿进树皮。

branches.en: The bird itself is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 鸟本身是字面义项。

branches.en: The repeated knocking sound gives a second sense.
branches.cn: 重复的敲击声给出第二个义项。

branches.en: A human figure for stubborn drilling and questioning.
branches.cn: 用人来比喻执着的凿问。

branches.en: The whole bird family shares the name.
branches.cn: 整个鸟科共享这个名字。

branches.en: Bird, sound, and family all come from the same beak-on-wood action.
branches.cn: 鸟、声音和鸟科都源于同一个「喙击木头」的动作。

intro.en: Woodpecker is a native English compound, built from the noun wood and the agent noun pecker, which is itself peck plus -er.
intro.cn: woodpecker 是英语本土复合词，由名词 wood 与施动名词 pecker 组成，而 pecker 本身又是 peck 加 -er。

latinIntro.en: Latin does not underlie the compound, but the scientific family name Picidae shares the same image of a pecking beak.
latinIntro.cn: 复合词底层没有拉丁语，但鸟科的学名 Picidae 来自拉丁语 picus（啄木鸟），同样取「啄」的意象。

items.example: Chickens peck at grain.
items.exampleCN: 鸡啄食谷粒。

items.example: The suffix -er forms pecker.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 pecker。

items.example: Pecker is the agent part of the compound.
items.exampleCN: pecker 是复合词中的施动部分。

items.example: Wood names what the bird works on.
items.exampleCN: wood 说明鸟加工的对象。

items.example: Woodpecker joins wood and pecker.
items.exampleCN: woodpecker 把 wood 与 pecker 合起来。

items.example: The suffix -s gives woodpeckers.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 woodpeckers。

items.meaningCN: 䴓：在树皮里夹开坚果的鸟
items.example: Nuthatch is built the same way.
items.exampleCN: nuthatch 用同样的方式构词。

items.meaning: a bird that creeps up trees
items.example: Treecreeper shows the same naming pattern.
items.exampleCN: treecreeper 体现同样的命名方式。

items.example: Latin picus is the family source.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 picus 是鸟科学名的来源。

definition_zh: 使恶化；变得更糟
definition_en: to become worse, or to make a situation, condition, or feeling worse than it already is
core_image: 一条本来向下倾斜的曲线，又被人往下压了一把
scene: 医生警告说，如果病人再抽烟，伤势会进一步恶化。The doctor warned that more smoking would worsen the patient condition.
sceneCN: 这里 worsen 是「使恶化」（第 1 个义项：让已经很糟的状况变得更糟）；句意：医生警告说，再抽烟会让病人的情况进一步恶化。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加动名词词尾构成，指恶化、加剧的过程或状态
比较级形式，义为「更糟的」，worsen 的形容词基础
最高级形式，义为「最糟的」，与 worse 同属一个系列
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「已经恶化的」

senses.title: To make a situation worse
senses.definition: to make an already bad situation, condition, or problem worse
senses.definitionCN: 让本已糟糕的情况、状况或问题变得更糟
senses.example: The heavy rain worsened the flooding in the low streets.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨使低洼街道的积水更加严重。
senses.why: The suffix -en turns an adjective into a verb meaning to make something have that quality, so worsen means to make it more worse.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -en 把形容词变成「使之具有该性质」的动词，所以 worsen 就是「使其更糟」。

senses.title: To become worse by itself
senses.definition: to get worse without an obvious outside cause, as a state or illness does
senses.definitionCN: 像病情或状态那样，在没有明显外因的情况下自行恶化
senses.example: His eyesight worsened slowly after he reached fifty.
senses.exampleCN: 他过了五十岁后视力慢慢变差了。
senses.why: Intransitive use lets the subject change on its own, so the same verb covers conditions that simply drift downward.
senses.whyCN: 不及物用法让主语自行变化，于是同一个动词也能描述那些只是不断下滑的状况。

senses.title: To make a person feel worse
senses.definition: to make someone feel more ill, upset, or uncomfortable
senses.definitionCN: 让某人的身体或情绪更不舒服、更难受
senses.example: The news worsened her mood for the rest of the day.
senses.exampleCN: 这个消息让她一整天的心情都更糟了。
senses.why: If a state can be made worse, then a mood or a body can be worsened too, because both are states a person carries.
senses.whyCN: 如果一种状况能被弄得更糟，那么心情和身体也就能被弄得更加难受，因为二者都是人自身的状态。

senses.title: To make relations or conditions more tense
senses.definition: to make relations between people or countries, or general conditions, more hostile or difficult
senses.definitionCN: 使人与人、国与国之间的关系或整体局势更对立、更艰难
senses.example: The new tax threatens to worsen trade relations between the two neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 新税项可能进一步激化这两个邻国之间的贸易关系。
senses.why: Relations and conditions are collective states, so a single action can push them further down the same worsening path.
senses.whyCN: 关系与局势都是集体性状态，因此一个动作就能把它们推上同一条继续恶化的道路。

intro.en: Worsen is a native English formation made from worse plus the verb suffix -en, a pattern also found in harden and quicken.
intro.cn: worsen 是英语本土构词，由 worse 加动词词尾 -en 组成，harden、quicken 用的是同一模式。

items.en: Wyrsa, a comparative of the word for evil, gives the ancestor of worse.
items.cn: 古英语 wyrsa 是表示「坏」的比较级形式，是 worse 的前身。

items.en: Werse takes its modern shape as an irregular comparative without the suffix -er.
items.cn: 中古英语 werse 定形为不带 -er 词尾的不规则比较级。

items.en: Wersen appears as an early verb meaning to grow or make worse; the spelling is recorded, the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为十三至十四世纪出现 wersen 这样的动词，义为变糟或使变糟；拼写有记录，具体首见年份存疑。

items.en: The form settles as worsen, following the pattern of harden and deepen.
items.cn: 一般认为十七世纪前后形式定为 worsen，与 harden、deepen 的模式一致。

items.en: Worsen becomes the standard verb for downward change in health, economy, and politics.
items.cn: 现代英语中 worsen 成为描述健康、经济、政治下滑的标准动词。

note.en: Worsen shares its root with worse, worst, and worse-sounding compounds, and it sits beside the near meanings decline, deteriorate, and aggravate.
note.cn: worsen 与 worse、worst 同根，并与 decline、deteriorate、aggravate 等近义词相邻。

entries.definition: the comparative of bad
entries.definitionCN: bad 的比较级；worsen 的直接基础词

entries.definition: the superlative of bad
entries.definitionCN: bad 的最高级；与 worse 同属一个系列

entries.definition: to make or become hard
entries.definitionCN: 使变硬；与 worsen 一样是形容词加 -en 构成的动词

entries.definition: to become worse in quality or condition
entries.definitionCN: 变坏、变质，比 worsen 更正式

entries.definition: to make an illness or problem worse
entries.definitionCN: 加重病情或问题，强调「使更严重」

entries.definition: to become less or lower over time
entries.definitionCN: 下降、衰退，侧重数量或水平的减少

normalIntro.en: See worsen as worse plus -en, the same ending that turns hard into harden and deep into deepen.
normalIntro.cn: 把 worsen 看成 worse 加 -en，正是把 hard 变 harden、把 deep 变 deepen 的那个词尾。

normal.en: The suffix -en means to make or become, so worsen means to make or become worse.
normal.cn: 词尾 -en 表示「使变得或变得」，所以 worsen 就是「使变糟或变糟」。

normal.en: The verb has both transitive and intransitive uses: a rain can worsen a fire, and a fire can worsen.
normal.cn: 这个词既可以及物也可以不及物：「雨水加剧火灾」与「火灾加剧」都能用它在句中表达。

normal.en: The past tense and past participle are both worsened, made with -ed.
normal.cn: 过去式和过去分词都是 worsened，直接加词尾 -ed。

normal.en: The present participle worsening is often used as an adjective before a noun.
normal.cn: 现在分词 worsening 常放在名词前作定语，如「恶化的状况」。

normal.en: In medical writing worsen and aggravate are close, but aggravate often names a specific worsening cause.
normal.cn: 在医学写作中 worsen 与 aggravate 相近，但 aggravate 往往点明具体的加重原因。

abstract.en: Picture a downward slope, and someone pushing a cart one step further down.
abstract.cn: 想象一段下坡路，有人把车又往坡下推了一步。

abstract.en: Imagine a small crack in a wall spreading into a much longer one.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上的一道小裂缝不断扩大，变成很长的一道。

abstract.en: Hear the sound of a bike scraping the ground as the road gets steeper.
abstract.cn: 想象山路变陡时，自行车刮地面的声音越来越刺耳。

examples.en: Lack of sleep can worsen an exam result far more than most students expect.
examples.cn: 睡眠不足对考试成绩的拖累往往比大多数学生想象的严重得多。

examples.en: Relations between the two countries worsened after the border incident.
examples.cn: 边境事件发生后，两国关系恶化了。

examples.en: If the wound gets wet, the infection may worsen quickly.
examples.cn: 伤口如果沾了水，感染可能会迅速加重。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我（wor）被沉（sen）下去了」——越来越糟就是往下沉；这只是拼音谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 wyrsa（更坏的）→ worse（bad 的比较级）+ 动词词尾 -en（使变得）→ worsen（使更糟；变糟）。

sensesIntro.en: Worsen moves from making a bad situation worse, through conditions that sink by themselves, to moods and relations that get tougher.
sensesIntro.cn: worsen 从「把糟糕的情况弄得更糟」开始，经自行下滑的状态，延伸到变得更难受的心情与更紧张的关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line already sloping down that is pushed even lower.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条本已向下的线，又被往下压了一截。

branches.en: The causative sense of making a bad thing worse.
branches.cn: 使糟糕之事更糟的致使义项。

branches.en: The intransitive sense of self-driven decline.
branches.cn: 自行下滑的不及物义项。

branches.en: A person mood or body made more uncomfortable.
branches.cn: 人的心情或身体变得更难受。

branches.en: Relations and collective conditions pushed further into conflict.
branches.cn: 关系与集体局势被进一步推向对立。

branches.en: All senses share the single downward move that -en turns into an action.
branches.cn: 所有义项共享同一个向下的移动，而 -en 把它变成了动作。

intro.en: Worsen is a native English verb formed from worse and the verbal suffix -en, with no borrowed prefix at all.
intro.cn: worsen 是英语本土动词，由 worse 与动词词尾 -en 构成，没有任何借来的前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin has no shared root; the nearest loan is the verb deteriorem facere, which yields the formal synonym deteriorate.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有共享的拉丁词根；最接近的借形是表示「使更坏」的拉丁动词，它后来带出正式同义词 deteriorate。

items.example: Worse is the base of the verb.
items.exampleCN: worse 是这个动词的基础。

items.example: The suffix -en turns adjectives into verbs.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -en 把形容词变成动词。

items.example: Worsen follows the pattern of harden.
items.exampleCN: worsen 遵循 harden 的模式。

items.example: The suffix -s gives worsens.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -s 构成 worsens。

items.example: The suffix -ed gives worsened.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 worsened。

items.example: The suffix -ing gives worsening.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 worsening。

items.example: Worsening appears in news reports.
items.exampleCN: worsening 常见于新闻报道。

items.example: Worst completes the comparison series.
items.exampleCN: worst 补齐了比较的系列。

items.example: Harden shows the same -en pattern.
items.exampleCN: harden 展示同样的 -en 构词方式。

definition_zh: 争论；口角；争吵；把……争取到手；把……设法弄到；放牧；看管（牲畜）
definition_en: to argue angrily about something for a long time, or to get something through long effort
core_image: 市场边两个人扯着一块布角，谁也不肯先松手
scene: 合同谈了一个上午，双方在分成比例上仍然各说各话，声音越来越大。The two firms wrangled for hours over the price of the land.
sceneCN: 这里 wrangle 是「争论、争个没完」（第 1 个义项：为某事争执不休）；句意：两家公司为这块地皮的价格争论了好几个小时。

derivatives.zh: 动词加 -er 构成的名词，指争吵者，在牧区也指照管马匹的人
动名词形式，指持续的争吵或激烈的讨价还价
牛仔文化中的牧马人，专指看管马群的骑手

senses.title: To argue angrily and at length
senses.definition: to argue with someone in an angry or noisy way for a long time
senses.definitionCN: 与某人激烈地争吵或长时间争论
senses.example: The neighbors wrangled over the boundary wall for years.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居们为这道界墙争执了好多年。
senses.why: The word comes from a story of quarrelling horses, so two parties pulling against each other are already in the picture.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自分马的故事，画面上本来就有两方互相拉扯，所以它自然表示各执一词的争吵。

senses.title: To obtain through effort
senses.definition: to get or win something after a long struggle or negotiation
senses.definitionCN: 经过长时间的争取或交涉才得到某物
senses.example: She wrangled a seat on the early flight.
senses.exampleCN: 她好不容易弄到了早班航班的座位。
senses.why: If two sides must struggle before one wins, the winner has literally pulled the thing toward himself, so effort becomes possession.
senses.whyCN: 既然两方要争到一方获胜，赢家等于是把东西拽向自己，于是「努力」就变成了「到手」。

senses.title: To herd or tend horses
senses.definition: to take care of horses or cattle, especially on open land
senses.definitionCN: 尤指在开阔牧场上照管马匹或牛群
senses.example: His grandfather wrangled horses in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 他的祖父曾在这个山谷里照管马匹。
senses.why: The oldest sense is to herd horses, and the modern meaning grew from that job of managing animals.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是「看管马匹」，今天通用的争论义正是从这份管牲畜的活计里长出来的。

senses.title: A noisy quarrel
senses.definition: a long, noisy, or complicated argument, often between groups
senses.definitionCN: 长时间、喧闹或复杂的争执，常发生于机构或团体之间
senses.example: The contract was delayed by a legal wrangle.
senses.exampleCN: 一场法律纠纷使合同一再推迟。
senses.why: English often turns a verb of quarrelling into a noun, naming the whole affair rather than the single exchange.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把争吵类动词转成名词，用来称呼整件事，而不只是其中的一次交锋。

intro.en: Wrangle probably grew from an early verb meaning to argue or struggle, recorded in English in the late fourteenth century.
intro.cn: wrangle 一般认为来自一个更早的动词，意为「争论、角力」，于十四世纪晚期出现在英语中。

items.en: A reconstructed form such as wrang, meaning something twisted or wrong, is often suggested as the starting point.
items.cn: 学者常推测，源头是一个意为「扭歪、犯错」的重构古英语形式。

items.en: Scandinavian words for wrestling and struggling may have reinforced the meaning.
items.cn: 北欧语言中表示「摔跤、角力」的词，可能强化了这一含义。

items.en: The verb is first recorded meaning to argue and struggle, and the noun follows soon after.
items.cn: 该动词最早记录为「争论、角力」，名词紧随其后出现。

items.en: The sense of herding horses is well attested in the American colonies.
items.cn: 在美洲殖民地，「看管马匹」的义项有充分记录。

items.en: Modern English keeps the horse sense in cowboy life and the arguing sense in legal and political writing.
items.cn: 现代英语在牛仔生活中保留牧马义，在法律与政治文字中则常用争论义。

note.en: Wrangle is a verb of prolonged argument, next to its noun and to wrestling, and near to everyday words for disagreement.
note.cn: wrangle 是表示「长时间争论」的动词，与同形的名词、wrestle 以及日常表示意见不合的词相邻。

entries.definition: a person who argues, or a person who herds horses
entries.definitionCN: 争吵的人；也指牧马人

entries.definition: long and noisy arguing
entries.definitionCN: 持续的争吵；讨价还价

entries.definition: to fight by holding and throwing, or to struggle hard
entries.definitionCN: 摔跤；奋力应付（与 wrangle 共享角力的意象，拼写相近但来源不同）

entries.definition: an angry argument between people who know each other
entries.definitionCN: 熟人之间的争吵

entries.definition: a serious disagreement, often official or legal
entries.definitionCN: 尤指正式或法律层面的争议

entries.definition: to discuss the terms of a deal
entries.definitionCN: 讨价还价；谈条件

normalIntro.en: Wrangle is the sound of two parties pulling the same rope and refusing to let go.
normalIntro.cn: wrangle 是两方各拉绳子一端、谁也不松手的画面。

normal.en: The old sense is herding horses, so a wrangler is also a cowboy who tends them.
normal.cn: 古义是看马，所以 wrangler 也指照管马匹的牛仔。

normal.en: Wrangle over a price means arguing about it for far too long.
normal.cn: wrangle over a price 是为价格吵到没完。

normal.en: The noun wrangle names the whole fight, as in a legal wrangle.
normal.cn: 名词 wrangle 指整场纷争，如 legal wrangle（法律纠纷）。

normal.en: To wrangle a ticket is to get one by insisting many times.
normal.cn: wrangle a ticket 是反复争取才弄到一张票。

normal.en: Compare with wrestle: both suggest effort, but wrangle stresses words and wrestle stresses the body.
normal.cn: 对比 wrestle：两者都含「用力」，但 wrangle 偏言语，wrestle 偏身体。

abstract.en: Imagine two lawyers pulling a single heavy document from opposite ends.
abstract.cn: 想象两位律师各拉一份厚文件的两端。

abstract.en: Picture a hand gripping something tight until the fingers turn white.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手死死攥住某物，指节都发白了。

abstract.en: Think of a rider circling a herd on a wide dusty plain.
abstract.cn: 想象一名骑手在尘土飞扬的平原上绕着一群马打转。

examples.en: Politicians wrangled over the budget until dawn.
examples.cn: 政客们为预算争论到天亮。

examples.en: He finally wrangled an invitation to the private viewing.
examples.cn: 他终于设法弄到了私人预展的邀请函。

examples.en: The settlement ended a long wrangle between the two firms.
examples.cn: 这次和解结束了两家公司之间漫长的纠纷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嚷过」——两个人一路嚷过去，谁也不服气，这就是争吵；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语早期形式（一般认为与表示「扭歪」的古英语形式有关）→ 十四世纪晚期的 wrangle（争论、角力）→ 现代英语的 wrangle，核心义「拉着不放、争到底」。

sensesIntro.en: Wrangle begins as an open argument, extends to getting something by fighting for it, keeps its old herding sense, and is also used as a noun for the whole affair.
sensesIntro.cn: wrangle 先从当面争吵说起，再延伸到靠自己争才到手，保留了古老的看牧义，也能作名词指整桩纠纷。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people holding one piece of cloth and pulling it from both ends.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人各执一块布的一端，互相拉扯。

branches.en: Long angry arguing is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 长时间激烈争吵是日常义项。

branches.en: Winning by effort is the pull turning into possession.
branches.cn: 靠力争而得，是拉扯变成了占有。

branches.en: Herding horses is the oldest recorded sense.
branches.cn: 看管马匹是最早有记录的义项。

branches.en: The noun and the verb both name the same fight.
branches.cn: 名词与动词指的是同一场争执。

branches.en: Managing animals and negotiating a deal both need patient skill.
branches.cn: 管好牲畜与谈成一笔交易，都需要耐心与技巧。

intro.en: Wrangle is a single Old English style stem, with wrangler and the gerund wrangling built around it, and no Latin prefix or suffix.
intro.cn: wrangle 是单一的英语词干，围绕它构成 wrangler 与动名词 wrangling，没有拉丁词缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin offers no direct relative, though the idea of wrestling has a separate Latin history.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中没有直接同源词，不过「摔跤、角力」这个概念在拉丁语里有另一段历史。

items.example: Wrangle is the base verb.
items.exampleCN: wrangle 是基础动词。

items.example: The noun wrangle keeps the verb meaning.
items.exampleCN: 名词 wrangle 保留动词含义。

items.example: The suffix -er forms wrangler.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 wrangler。

items.example: Wrangler names the person.
items.exampleCN: wrangler 指人。

items.example: The suffix -ling forms wrangling.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ling 构成 wrangling。

items.example: Wrangling names the activity.
items.exampleCN: wrangling 指这一活动。

items.example: They wrangle over details.
items.exampleCN: 他们为细节争论。

items.example: She wrangled with the manager.
items.exampleCN: 她与经理争辩。

items.example: He wrangled a deal at last.
items.exampleCN: 他终于谈成了一笔交易。

definition_zh: 愤怒；暴怒；愤慨；复仇的怒火；惩罚
definition_en: extreme anger, often a formal or literary kind that looks for punishment
core_image: 一张涨红的脸俯下来，拳头攥得关节发白
scene: 谈判桌上，对方一次次推翻已经说好的条件，老人沉默很久，终于拍案而起。His wrath was terrible when he learned of the betrayal.
sceneCN: 这里 wrath 是「暴怒」（第 1 个义项：强烈而想要惩罚对方的怒气）；句意：当他得知这场背叛时，他的怒火可怕极了。

derivatives.zh: 加 -ful 构成的形容词，意为「愤怒的；怒气冲冲的」
wrathful 加 -ly 构成的副词，意为「愤怒地」
与 wrath 同源的古语形容词，意为「愤怒的」，多见于较早期文本

senses.title: Intense anger
senses.definition: a very strong feeling of anger that demands a response
senses.definitionCN: 强烈得需要有所回应的愤怒情绪
senses.example: The villagers lived in fear of the royal wrath.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们在国王的怒火下战战兢兢地生活。
senses.why: The word descends from a root meaning hot and twisting, so anger appears as heat boiling inside a person.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自表示「炽热、扭动」的词根，于是愤怒被写成在体内沸腾的热。

senses.title: Punishment for wrongdoing
senses.definition: the punishment or attack that follows a serious wrong
senses.definitionCN: 因严重过错而招来的惩罚或打击
senses.example: The inspectors brought the wrath of the regulator upon the firm.
senses.exampleCN: 检查人员使这家公司招来了监管机构的严厉惩处。
senses.why: Because wrath is anger that wants to be answered, the result of that answer, punishment, borrows the same word.
senses.whyCN: 因为 wrath 是想要得到回应的怒气，这种回应落实下来就是惩罚，于是同一个词也指惩罚本身。

senses.title: The wrath of nature
senses.definition: the destructive force of a storm, flood, or other natural event
senses.definitionCN: 风暴、洪水等自然现象的毁灭性力量
senses.example: The old lighthouse has survived the wrath of many storms.
senses.exampleCN: 那座老灯塔经受了许多风暴的肆虐。
senses.why: A person in wrath strikes without mercy, so writers picture a storm as an angry giant doing the same.
senses.whyCN: 暴怒的人下手毫不留情，于是作家把风暴设想成一个发怒的巨人。

senses.title: Anger of a deity or ruler
senses.definition: the anger attributed to a god or to a powerful authority
senses.definitionCN: 归于神祇或权力拥有者的怒火
senses.example: In the ancient tale the flood was sent as divine wrath.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个古老传说里，洪水被当作神怒降下。
senses.why: Religious and royal writing made wrath a word for anger that strikes from above, which fixed its solemn tone.
senses.whyCN: 宗教与王室文本让 wrath 专指从高处落下的怒火，这也奠定了它庄重的语气。

intro.en: Wrath is one of the oldest English words for anger, with relatives in several Germanic languages.
intro.cn: wrath 是英语中表示愤怒最古老的词之一，在多种日耳曼语中有同源词。

items.en: A reconstructed form with a sense of twisting or raging lies behind the word.
items.cn: 一般认为其背后是一个含「扭动、狂暴」意味的重构日耳曼语形式。

items.en: The old noun means anger and rage, but also the fury of weather or illness.
items.cn: 古英语名词既指愤怒，也指天气或疾病的狂暴。

items.en: The word narrows to anger, especially the anger of God, kings, or fathers.
items.cn: 中古英语时期词义收窄为愤怒，尤指神、国王或父亲的怒火。

items.en: Bible translation fixes the phrase the day of wrath in religious language.
items.cn: 圣经英译把「震怒之日」一类说法固定下来，使其进入宗教语言。

items.en: Modern English keeps wrath mainly in formal, literary, and journalistic use.
items.cn: 现代英语中 wrath 主要用于正式、文学与新闻语体。

note.en: Wrath is the solemn word for anger, standing beside angry and wroth, and close to the everyday words anger and ire.
note.cn: wrath 是表示愤怒的庄重用词，与 angry、wroth 同族，意义接近日常的 anger 与 ire。

entries.definition: angry, now archaic
entries.definitionCN: 愤怒的（现已古旧）

entries.definition: full of anger
entries.definitionCN: 愤怒的；怒气冲冲的

entries.definition: a ring of flowers or leaves
entries.definitionCN: 花环；花圈（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: the general feeling of being annoyed
entries.definitionCN: 泛指发怒的情绪

entries.definition: anger, used in formal or humorous writing
entries.definitionCN: 愤怒（正式或戏谑用法）

entries.definition: violent uncontrolled anger
entries.definitionCN: 狂怒；暴怒

normalIntro.en: Wrath is heat held behind a locked door, quiet at first and then sudden.
normalIntro.cn: wrath 是关在门后的热，先安静，然后猛然冲出。

normal.en: The adjective wrathful keeps the noun inside it, as in a wrathful face.
normal.cn: 形容词 wrathful 内含这个名词，如 wrathful face（怒容）。

normal.en: To incur the wrath of someone is to make that person very angry.
normal.cn: incur the wrath of 某人，就是招来某人的怒火。

normal.en: Wrath is stronger and more formal than anger; for everyday cases choose anger.
normal.cn: wrath 比 anger 更重也更正式，日常小事用 anger 才自然。

normal.en: The old adjective wroth uses the same ending as the noun wrath.
normal.cn: 古旧形容词 wroth 与名词 wrath 共用同样的词尾。

normal.en: Bible English fixed the phrase the day of wrath for judgment.
normal.cn: 圣经英译用 the day of wrath 指审判之日。

abstract.en: Imagine a kettle whose lid is shaking as the water boils.
abstract.cn: 想象水烧开时，壶盖被顶得直颤。

abstract.en: Picture a raised hand that is about to come down.
abstract.cn: 想象一只高高抬起、正要落下的手。

abstract.en: Think of black clouds piling up before a great storm.
abstract.cn: 想象大风暴来临前越堆越厚的黑云。

examples.en: The decision drew the wrath of local residents.
examples.cn: 这一决定引来了当地居民的愤怒。

examples.en: He feared the wrath of his father more than any punishment.
examples.cn: 他怕父亲的怒火，胜过怕任何惩罚。

examples.en: The ship lay quiet after the wrath of the storm had passed.
examples.cn: 风暴的狂暴过去后，船静静地躺在那里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「若死」——气到极点几乎要命，就是暴怒；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 重构日耳曼语词根（一般认为含「扭动、狂暴」义）→ 古英语 wrath（愤怒；狂暴）→ 中古英语 wrath（多指神、王、父之怒），核心义「要把怒气讨回来的强烈愤怒」。

sensesIntro.en: Wrath starts as intense anger, then names the punishment that anger brings, spreads to the violence of nature, and is fixed in religious language for divine anger.
sensesIntro.cn: wrath 先从强烈的愤怒说起，再指这种怒气带来的惩罚，又延伸到自然力的狂暴，最后在宗教语言中固定为神怒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a reddened face looking down, fists clenched until the knuckles are white.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张涨红的脸俯视着，拳头攥得指节发白。

branches.en: Intense anger is the central sense.
branches.cn: 强烈愤怒是中心义项。

branches.en: Punishment is anger that has been carried out.
branches.cn: 惩罚是落实了的怒气。

branches.en: The violence of a storm borrows the human feeling.
branches.cn: 风暴的狂暴借用了人的情绪。

branches.en: Anger that strikes from above keeps its solemn tone.
branches.cn: 自高处落下的怒火保留了庄重语气。

branches.en: Both a punishment and a flood arrive with force that cannot be argued with.
branches.cn: 惩罚与洪水都以无法辩驳的力量降临。

intro.en: Wrath is a native English noun with the adjective wrathful and the older wroth built on the same stem.
intro.cn: wrath 是英语本族名词，同一词干上构成形容词 wrathful 与更古旧的 wroth。

latinIntro.en: Wrath has no Latin ancestor, though Latin has a separate noun for anger, ira.
latinIntro.cn: wrath 没有拉丁语祖先，不过拉丁语另有一个表示愤怒的名词 ira。

items.example: Wrath is the oldest layer of the word.
items.exampleCN: wrath 是这个单词最古老的部分。

items.example: The suffix -ful forms wrathful.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ful 构成 wrathful。

items.example: Wrathful describes the angry person.
items.exampleCN: wrathful 形容愤怒的人。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms wrathfully.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 wrathfully。

items.example: Wrathfully modifies the verb.
items.exampleCN: wrathfully 修饰动词。

items.example: Wroth is an old adjective form.
items.exampleCN: wroth 是古老的形容词形式。

items.example: They feared the wrath of the crowd.
items.exampleCN: 他们害怕人群的怒火。

items.example: He incurred the wrath of the board.
items.exampleCN: 他招来了董事会的震怒。

items.example: Righteous wrath drove the protest.
items.exampleCN: 义愤推动了那场抗议。

definition_zh: 残骸；碎片；废墟；毁坏状态；（计划等的）残局
definition_en: the broken parts of a destroyed ship, plane, building, or vehicle
core_image: 被砸碎的船身散落在浪边，木板与铁片斜插在沙里
scene: 台风过后的清晨，人们围在岸边，看着半截船身搁浅在礁石旁。Divers searched the wreckage for the black box.
sceneCN: 这里 wreckage 是「残骸」（第 1 个义项：撞毁或沉没后剩下的破碎部分）；句意：潜水员在残骸中搜寻黑匣子。

collocations.zh: 从残骸中获救的生还者

derivatives.zh: 加 -age 所依据的基础名词，意为「失事的船或车；毁坏」
与名词同形的基础动词，意为「毁坏；使失事」
由 wreck 加 -er 构成，指造成破坏者，也指救援拖车

senses.title: Broken remains of a disaster
senses.definition: the parts left of a ship, plane, building, or vehicle after it is destroyed
senses.definitionCN: 船只、飞机、建筑或车辆被毁后留下的部分
senses.example: Rescuers pulled two children from the wreckage.
senses.exampleCN: 救援人员从残骸中救出了两个孩子。
senses.why: Wreck names a destroyed vessel, and the suffix -age gathers a mass of things, so wreckage is the whole broken pile.
senses.whyCN: wreck 指失事的船，后缀 -age 表示成堆的物，合起来便是那一片破碎的堆积物。

senses.title: Ruined surroundings
senses.definition: an area of ground covered with the broken remains of a building
senses.definitionCN: 散落着建筑残骸的一片地面
senses.example: Volunteers cleared the wreckage of the collapsed wall.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者清理了倒塌围墙留下的废墟。
senses.why: The same gathered notion applies to a town or a street, so the word moves from a single object to a whole place.
senses.whyCN: 同一种「成堆」的概念也适用于街区与城镇，于是词义从单个物件扩展到一整片地方。

senses.title: A ruined state
senses.definition: the state of being ruined, especially of a career or an organization
senses.definitionCN: 被毁坏的状态，尤指事业或组织的残破
senses.example: The manager inspected the wreckage of his career.
senses.exampleCN: 这位经理检视着自己事业的残局。
senses.why: -age also names a condition, as in breakage, so wreckage can describe how ruined something is rather than what it is made of.
senses.whyCN: -age 也能表示状态（如 breakage），所以 wreckage 可以描述毁坏的程度，而不只是那些碎片本身。

senses.title: Leftovers of a failed plan
senses.definition: what is left of plans, ideas, or hopes that have failed
senses.definitionCN: 失败的计划、想法或希望所剩下的东西
senses.example: Journalists picked through the wreckage of the peace deal.
senses.exampleCN: 记者们仔细梳理那份和平协议的残局。
senses.why: If a ship can be wrecked, so can an agreement, and its leftovers borrow the picture of scattered pieces.
senses.whyCN: 船会失事，协议也会崩盘，剩下的东西就借用了碎片散落的画面。

intro.en: Wreckage is a compound built in English from wreck and the suffix -age, recorded in the sixteenth century for what has been wrecked.
intro.cn: wreckage 是英语内部用 wreck 加后缀 -age 构成的复合词，十六世纪记录为「被毁之物」。

items.en: A Scandinavian word for a wrecked ship or floating timber gives English wreck.
items.cn: 北欧语言中表示「失事船只、漂流木料」的词，为英语提供了 wreck。

items.en: Wreck enters English through contacts with northern seafarers.
items.cn: wreck 经由与北方航海者的接触进入英语。

items.en: Wreckage is formed with the French style suffix -age, meaning a mass of wrecked things.
items.cn: wreckage 加上源自法语的后缀 -age 构成，指成堆的毁坏之物。

items.en: The word spreads from shipping reports to railways and then to air crashes.
items.cn: 这个词从航运报道扩展到铁路，再扩展到空难报道。

items.en: Modern English also uses it as a figure for ruined plans and careers.
items.cn: 现代英语又用它比喻破灭的计划与事业。

note.en: Wreckage is the gathered mass left by a wreck, standing beside wreck and reckoning, and near to debris and rubble.
note.cn: wreckage 是 wreck 之后堆积起来的破碎物，与 wreck、reckoning 相邻，意义接近 debris 与 rubble。

entries.definition: a destroyed ship, or to destroy something
entries.definitionCN: 失事的船；毁坏

entries.definition: a calculation or a time of settling accounts
entries.definitionCN: 计算；清算（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a person or vehicle that removes or causes wrecks
entries.definitionCN: 造成破坏者；救援拖车

entries.definition: scattered pieces left after damage
entries.definitionCN: 残片；碎片

entries.definition: broken stones and bricks from a building
entries.definitionCN: 碎石；瓦砾

entries.definition: the parts that are left of something
entries.definitionCN: 剩余物；遗迹

normalIntro.en: Wreckage is wreck with a heap at the end: something was broken, and the broken parts stayed.
normalIntro.cn: wreckage 就是 wreck 后面多了一堆东西：东西碎了，碎片还留在原处。

normal.en: Wreck is the base word, so wreckage means what a wreck leaves behind.
normal.cn: wreck 是基础词，wreckage 就是失事之后留下的东西。

normal.en: The suffix -age often means a mass, as in baggage or voltage.
normal.cn: 后缀 -age 常表示成堆的量，如 baggage 与 voltage。

normal.en: Reporters say amid the wreckage when they mean inside the broken remains.
normal.cn: 记者常用 amid the wreckage，表示在残骸之中。

normal.en: Wreckage is uncountable in ordinary use, so avoid a wreckage unless it has a qualifier.
normal.cn: wreckage 通常不可数，前面加冠词时要带修饰语。

normal.en: Compare with wreck: the wreck is the ruined object, the wreckage is the pile of its parts.
normal.cn: 对比 wreck：wreck 指毁了的整个物体，wreckage 指它散落成的一堆碎片。

abstract.en: Picture a metal sheet bent into a curve on wet sand.
abstract.cn: 想象一块金属板在湿沙上弯成弧形。

abstract.en: Imagine walking over broken glass and brick after a wall falls.
abstract.cn: 想象墙塌之后，你踩过碎砖烂瓦。

abstract.en: Think of a desk after a contract falls apart, papers everywhere.
abstract.cn: 想象一份合同崩盘后的办公桌，文件散得到处都是。

examples.en: Firefighters searched the wreckage for survivors.
examples.cn: 消防员在残骸中搜寻生还者。

examples.en: The road was blocked by wreckage from the crash.
examples.cn: 道路被撞车留下的残骸堵住了。

examples.en: The town spent a year clearing the wreckage of the flood.
examples.cn: 小镇花了一年时间清理洪水留下的废墟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「芮克基」——船撞上礁石碎成一片，这堆碎片就是残骸；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古诺斯语（一般认为与表示「失事船只、漂流木」的词相关）→ 英语 wreck（失事船只；毁坏）→ wreck + -age（成堆、状态）→ wreckage，核心义「毁坏之后堆下的残片」。

sensesIntro.en: Wreckage starts with the physical remains of a destroyed object, covers a whole ruined area, names the ruined state itself, and ends as a figure for ruined plans.
sensesIntro.cn: wreckage 先从被毁物件留下的实物残片说起，再指一整片废墟，也指毁坏状态本身，最后比喻破灭的计划。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a smashed hull lying in the shallows, boards and iron plates stuck in the sand.
core.cn: 核心意象：砸碎的船身躺在浅滩，木板与铁片斜插在沙里。

branches.en: The physical remains are the central sense.
branches.cn: 实物残骸是中心义项。

branches.en: A ruined area is the remains stretched over ground.
branches.cn: 废墟是摊开在地面上的一片残骸。

branches.en: The ruined state is the condition left behind.
branches.cn: 毁坏状态是残骸留下的境况。

branches.en: A ship and a street both leave the same kind of scattered mass.
branches.cn: 船体与街巷都留下同样散落的堆积物。

branches.en: A ruined career and a failed deal share the abstract picture.
branches.cn: 毁掉的事业与崩掉的交易共用这类抽象画面。

intro.en: Wreckage is built from the English noun wreck plus the suffix -age, and the family also gives wreck, wrecker, and wrecked.
intro.cn: wreckage 由英语名词 wreck 加后缀 -age 构成，同一词族还有 wreck、wrecker 与 wrecked。

latinIntro.en: The suffix -age is traced through French to Latin, where it ended in -aticum.
latinIntro.cn: 后缀 -age 经法语溯至拉丁语，其拉丁形式以 -aticum 结尾。

items.example: Wreck is the base noun.
items.exampleCN: wreck 是基础名词。

items.meaningCN: 表示集合或状态的词尾
items.example: The suffix -age forms wreckage.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -age 构成 wreckage。

items.example: The suffix came through Old French.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾经古法语传来。

items.example: Wreckage keeps the base meaning.
items.exampleCN: wreckage 保留基础词义。

items.example: The suffix -er forms wrecker.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 wrecker。

items.meaning: a destroyer or a rescue vehicle
items.example: Wrecker names the agent.
items.exampleCN: wrecker 指施动者。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms wrecked.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 wrecked。

items.example: Wrecked describes the object.
items.exampleCN: wrecked 形容物体。

items.example: Wrecking names the action.
items.exampleCN: wrecking 指破坏这一行为。

latinEntries.exampleCN: 它构成了现代后缀 -age 的源头。

definition_zh: 摔跤；扭打；奋力对付；绞尽脑汁思考；搏斗；扭夺
definition_en: to fight by holding and twisting an opponent, or to struggle hard with a problem or decision
core_image: 两个人抱住对方，手臂绞在一起，用力把对手往地上压
scene: 场地中央只铺了一块旧垫子，两侧的人紧紧抱住彼此，谁都不肯松手。They try hard to wrestle each other down before the referee counts.
sceneCN: 这里 wrestle 是「摔跤、扭打」（第 1 个义项：抱住对手用力把他摔倒）；句意为摔跤手再一次抓住对方，想在裁判数秒之前逼出一次倒地。

pos.zh: （与问题、情感）艰苦斗争；绞尽脑汁

collocations.zh: 费力争斗；艰难对付（问题、情感）

derivatives.zh: 由 wrestle 加 -er 「做某事的人」构成，义为「摔跤手」
由 wrestle 加 -ing 构成，义为「摔跤运动、扭斗」
由 wrist 「手腕」+ lock 「锁」构成，指摔跤中锁住对手手腕的招法

senses.title: To fight by gripping and throwing
senses.definition: to fight someone by holding on to them and trying to throw or force them down
senses.definitionCN: 抱住某人、用力把他摔倒或压在地上的搏斗
senses.example: The two boys wrestled on the grass until their father pulled them apart.
senses.exampleCN: 两个男孩在草地上扭打，直到父亲把他们拉开。
senses.why: The Old English verb wræstan first meant to twist or wrench, so two bodies gripping and turning each other is the original picture.
senses.whyCN: 古英语动词 wræstan 本义是「扭、拧」，两人抱住彼此相互翻转，正对应这个词最初的画面。

senses.title: To struggle hard with a problem
senses.definition: to try very hard to deal with a difficult problem, question, or decision
senses.definitionCN: 费力地应对难题、问题或重大决定
senses.example: For weeks she wrestled with the question of whether to leave her job.
senses.exampleCN: 有好几个星期，她一直在苦苦思索是否该辞掉工作。
senses.why: A problem can be felt as an opponent: the mind grips it, turns it over, and refuses to let go, just as a fighter does.
senses.whyCN: 难题可以被感受为一个对手：头脑抓住它、反复翻转、不肯放手，和摔跤手较劲一模一样。

senses.title: To resist an inner force
senses.definition: to fight against a feeling, a temptation, or a duty inside yourself
senses.definitionCN: 在内心深处与情绪、诱惑或责任搏斗
senses.example: He wrestled with his conscience all night before he went to the police.
senses.exampleCN: 去警察局之前，他整夜都在跟自己的良心搏斗。
senses.why: If the opponent is invisible, the struggle moves inside the body, and conscience or fear becomes the thing to be pinned down.
senses.whyCN: 当对手看不见时，角力就移到了身体内部，良心或恐惧成了那个被按住的东西。

senses.title: To twist or pull something free
senses.definition: to twist or pull something, often to get it away from someone
senses.definitionCN: 用力扭动或拉扯某物，常指从别人手里夺过来
senses.example: She wrestled the heavy lid off the jar with both hands.
senses.exampleCN: 她双手用力绞拧，才把罐子那沉重的盖子拧开。
senses.why: The ancient sense of wrenching something loose survives in this verb: the strength is applied to an object instead of a person.
senses.whyCN: 「把东西硬拧下来」这一古老含义仍保留在这个动词里：力气使在物件身上，而不是人身上。

senses.title: To argue or contend over something
senses.definition: to fight or argue with others in order to gain control of something
senses.definitionCN: 为了掌控某物而与他人争斗或争论
senses.example: The three companies wrestled over the contract for the new airport.
senses.exampleCN: 三家公司为了新机场的那份合同争执不休。
senses.why: Two sides pulling one prize is a social version of the grapple: the object in the middle is the opponent now.
senses.whyCN: 两方争抢同一个目标，是角力的社会版本：如今中间那个诱人的事物成了对手。

senses.title: The sport and the contest
senses.definition: the sport of wrestling, or a hard contest of physical strength
senses.definitionCN: 摔跤这项运动，或一场激烈的体力较量
senses.example: Wrestling has been an Olympic sport since ancient times.
senses.exampleCN: 摔跤自古以来就是奥运项目。
senses.why: When the action became a lasting institution, the -ing noun and the plain verb were used for the sport itself.
senses.whyCN: 当这个动作固化为一项长期存在的项目，-ing 形式和原形动词就被用来指这项运动本身。

senses.title: A hard contest in any field
senses.definition: a hard, determined effort to overcome a difficulty or an opponent
senses.definitionCN: 为克服困难或对手而进行的艰苦而坚决的努力
senses.example: Getting the bridge reopened was a long wrestle with the city council.
senses.exampleCN: 让这座桥重新开放，是和市议会之间一场旷日持久的较量。
senses.why: Once the struggle leaves the mat, the noun name the whole long fight with red tape, budget, or weather.
senses.whyCN: 一旦拼斗离开垫子，这个名词就能指与官僚程序、预算或天气的整场漫长搏斗。

intro.en: Wrestle goes back to Old English wræstan, to twist or wrench, a word of uncertain deeper origin.
intro.cn: wrestle 可追溯到古英语 wræstan（扭、拧），更早的来源目前无法确定。

items.en: Wrestle swears wræstan, meaning to twist or wrench, and is first recorded in Old English.
items.cn: wrestle 源于 wræstan，意为扭、拧，最早见于古英语。

items.en: The older noun wraxlian, meaning to wrestle, shows the fighting sense already in place.
items.cn: 更早的动词 wraxlian 意为摔跤，说明搏斗义当时已经确立。

items.en: The form becomes wrestlen, with the loss of the final vowel of the infinitive.
items.cn: 这一形式演变为 wrestlen，不定式词尾的元音脱落。

items.en: The wrestling match becomes a popular fairground sport in England.
items.cn: 在英格兰，摔跤比赛成为集市上广受欢迎的竞技项目。

items.en: The word is applied to sport, to wrestling with a problem, and to contests of any kind.
items.cn: 这个词被用于体育项目、费心对付难题，以及各种形式的较量。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with a similar initial shape or a shared twisting root; the near-meaning group gathers other verbs of close combat or of mental struggle.
note.cn: 形近组收开头写法相近或共享「扭」这一词根的词；近义组收表示近身搏斗或艰难思索的其他动词。

entries.definition: The joint between the hand and the arm; it only looks similar in spelling and comes from a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「手腕」；只是与这个词开头拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To twist the body about in pain or struggle; built on the same ancient twisting idea.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「扭动、翻滚」，多因疼痛或挣扎而扭动身体；与这个词共享古老的「扭」义。

entries.definition: A rare verb formed from wrestle, meaning to wrench or twist free; rarely used today.
entries.definitionCN: 由这个词派生出的罕见动词，义为「扭挣脱开」，今天几乎不用。

entries.definition: To seize and hold someone in close combat; also used of struggling with a problem.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「扭打、抓牢」，也用于与难题较劲，与这个词几乎可以互换，但略显正式。

entries.definition: To make a violent effort against something; more general and not limited to gripping.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「挣扎、奋斗」，范围更宽，不限于贴身纠缠。

entries.definition: A short, untidy fight or scramble; more casual and less serious than a wrestling bout.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「扭打、争抢」，比正式的比赛较轻、较随意。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English root, the word family, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子基于真实的古英语词根、同族词，以及这个词实际出现的常见搭配。

normal.en: The silent w puts the sound at the front: wrestle, wring and wrinkle all begin in sound with a simple r.
normal.cn: 开头那个不发音的 w 让这个词读起来以简单的 r 音起头：wrestle、wring、wrinkle 都是如此。

normal.en: Wrestle with a problem means turning it over in your mind, as a wrestler turns his opponent.
normal.cn: wrestle with a problem 指在头脑里反复掂量它，就像摔跤手翻转对手一样。

normal.en: A wrestler is the person and wrestling is the sport; the simple verb names the action.
normal.cn: wrestler 指摔跤手，wrestling 指摔跤运动，而简单的动词原形本身就表示这个动作。

normal.en: Arm-wrestling is the smallest version of the fight: two hands locked and pushed against each other.
normal.cn: 扳手腕是这种角力最小的版本：两只手扣在一起互相推。

normal.en: Compare grapple: grapple can join a boat to another or take hold of a rock, but wrestle keeps the image of two bodies.
normal.cn: 对比 grapple：grapple 可以表示把两条船连住或抓住岩石，而 wrestle 始终保留两个身体的画面。

abstract.en: Picture two arms locked together, straining, neither giving way.
abstract.cn: 想象两条胳膊绞在一起，青筋绷紧，谁也不退让。

abstract.en: Picture a decision held up in the air, twisted first one way and then the other, before it finally drops.
abstract.cn: 想象一个决定被悬在半空，先往这边拧、再往那边拧，最后才落下来。

abstract.en: Picture someone alone at night, fighting invisible hands inside their chest.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人深夜独坐，在胸腔里与看不见的手较劲。

examples.en: The two farmers wrestled in the yard over the broken fence.
examples.cn: 两个农民在院子里为了那堵破篱笆扭打起来。

examples.en: Investors are still wrestling with the risks of the new sector.
examples.cn: 投资者仍在为这个新行业的风险而苦苦思索。

examples.en: Getting the plane landing approved was a year-long wrestle with the authorities.
examples.cn: 让这架飞机获得着陆许可，是和当局长达一年的苦苦较量。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞索」——两个人互相揪住，谁也不肯松手的「死死较劲」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 wræstan「扭、拧」→ 中古英语 wrestlen → 现代英语 wrestle；核心义是「相互扭住、较劲」，因而从摔跤扩展到与难题、与内心的搏斗。更早的词源来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Wrestle begins with two bodies twisting each other, then moves the same struggle into the mind, then names the long contest itself.
sensesIntro.cn: wrestle 从两个人互相翻转身体开始，接着把这种较劲搬进头脑里，最后用来指那一整场漫长的较量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two arms locked together, both bodies straining and turning.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条胳膊绞在一起，两具身体绷紧、相互翻转。

branches.en: The literal fight on the mat is the first sense and the sport built from it.
branches.cn: 垫子上的真实搏斗是第一个义项，也是由此形成的运动项目。

branches.en: The opponent moves inside the mind as a problem or a feeling to be overcome.
branches.cn: 对手移进头脑，变成需要克服的难题或情绪。

branches.en: Twisting a lid or a stick is the old wrenching sense acting on an object.
branches.cn: 拧开盖子或拧拗棍子，是古老的「扭拧」义作用在物件上。

branches.en: Contesting a contract or a project is the same struggle played out between rivals.
branches.cn: 争夺合同或项目，是同一种搏斗在对手之间的上演。

branches.en: A short scuffle and a long wrestle with officials both use one image, only the length changes.
branches.cn: 短暂扭打与和政府部门的长期较量用的是同一幅画面，只是时间长短不同。

intro.en: Wrestle has little affix material: its -le ending belongs to the Middle English verb ending -len, and the word family is built mainly with -er and -ing.
intro.cn: wrestle 能拆出的词缀材料很少：结尾的 -le 属于中古英语动词词尾 -len，同族词主要靠 -er 与 -ing 构成。

latinIntro.en: Wrestle is a native English word with no Latin ancestor; the Latin entries below are only related words of the same wrestling and wrenching field.
latinIntro.cn: wrestle 是英语本族词，没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁同族词只是摔跤与扭拧义场中的相关词。

items.example: Wræstan is the Old English ancestor of wrestle.
items.exampleCN: wræstan 是 wrestle 的古英语祖先。

items.example: Wraxlian already carries the sporting sense.
items.exampleCN: wraxlian 已经带有竞技的含义。

items.meaning: a frequentative verb ending, suggesting repeated action
items.meaningCN: 动词词尾，表示反复进行的动作
items.example: The ending -le in wrestle echoes a repeated twisting motion.
items.exampleCN: wrestle 里的 -le 呼应反复扭动的动作。

items.meaning: to pull away by force, to twist
items.example: Wrest keeps the bare twisting sense without the fight.
items.exampleCN: wrest 保留纯粹的扭拧义，不带格斗。

items.example: The suffix -er forms wrestler from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 由这个动词构成 wrestler。

items.meaning: a person regarded as having a quality
items.meaningCN: 指具有某种特征的人的词尾
items.example: Wrestling uses -ing to name the sport.
items.exampleCN: wrestling 用 -ing 来指这项运动。

items.example: The phrase wrestle with marks the opponent.
items.exampleCN: 短语 wrestle with 标出了较劲的对象。

items.meaning: an initial spelling with a silent w
items.meaningCN: 带不发音 w 的开头字母组合
items.example: The starting letters in wring and writhe are silent too.
items.exampleCN: wring 和 writhe 开头的字母组合同样不发音。

definition_zh: 可怜的人；不幸的人；可恶的人；卑鄙小人；流放者；被逐出者
definition_en: an unhappy or unfortunate person, or a person one despises for being mean or cruel
core_image: 一个衣衫褴褛的人蜷缩在路边，被风推着、被众人赶着离开家园
scene: 雨夜里街角蜷着一个衣衫湿透的人，行人绕着他快步走过。Only a poor wretch was left sitting in the rain outside the closed market.
sceneCN: 这里 wretch 是「可怜的人、不幸的人」（第 1 个义项：处境悲惨、值得同情的人）；句意为只有一个可怜人还坐在关闭的集市门口淋着雨。

derivatives.zh: 由 wretch 加 -ed 构成，义为「悲惨的、不幸的、恶劣的」
由 wretched 加 -ness 构成，义为「悲惨、不幸」
古旧形式，见于早期英语宗教文本，义为「冷酷无情」

senses.title: An unfortunate person
senses.definition: a person who is unhappy, unlucky, or in great distress
senses.definitionCN: 不快乐、遭遇不幸或处境极度艰难的人
senses.example: The old wretch sat on the steps with no coat and no home.
senses.exampleCN: 那个可怜的老人坐在台阶上，没有外套，也没有家。
senses.why: The word began as a name for an exile, so the picture of someone cast out is still under every plea for the poor wretch.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指被逐出者，所以「被抛弃的人」这一画面始终藏在每一句 poor wretch 的叹息里。

senses.title: A despicable person
senses.definition: a person whom the speaker despises as mean, cruel, or worthless
senses.definitionCN: 说话者鄙视其卑鄙、残忍或毫无价值的人
senses.example: You ungrateful wretch, after all the help I gave you.
senses.exampleCN: 你这个忘恩负义的家伙，我帮了你那么多。
senses.why: The same exile view flips: if a person deserves to be driven out, the word becomes an insult rather than pity.
senses.whyCN: 「被逐出者」的视角一反转：如果某人活该被赶走，这个词就从同情变成了谩骂。

senses.title: A poor or humble creature
senses.definition: a humble, poor, or powerless being, often said with pity or gentle humour
senses.definitionCN: 卑微、贫穷或无力的人或生物，常带怜悯或温和的玩笑语气
senses.example: The little wretch was still awake at midnight, reading under the blanket.
senses.exampleCN: 那个小家伙到午夜还没睡，蒙在被子里看书。
senses.why: Once the word stopped naming only adults, it was stretched to children and animals that seem helpless.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词不再只指成年人，它就被延伸用到看起来很无助的孩子和动物身上。

senses.title: A person cast out
senses.definition: a person who has been driven away from home or society
senses.definitionCN: 被赶离家园或被社会排斥的人
senses.example: The chronicle calls the brothers rebels, wretches, and traitors in one breath.
senses.exampleCN: 那份编年史一口气把这对兄弟称作叛党、流放者和叛徒。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: the Germanic noun describes someone driven out of the land.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项：日耳曼语名词指的就是被赶出土地的人。

senses.title: A miserable state
senses.definition: a state of great misery and helplessness, often as a thing said of a life or a place
senses.definitionCN: 极度痛苦和无助的境地，常用来形容一种生活或一个地方
senses.example: The hovel showed the wretch of a life the family had been forced to live.
senses.exampleCN: 那间破屋显出了一家人被迫过的悲惨生活。
senses.why: When the noun joins a phrase like a life or a place, the person fades and only the misery is left.
senses.whyCN: 当这个名词修饰「生活」或「地方」时，人就退场了，只剩下悲惨本身。

senses.title: A figure of pathos
senses.definition: a pitiable figure used in songs, hymns, and literature to draw sympathy
senses.definitionCN: 歌曲、赞美诗和文学中用来唤起同情的可怜角色
senses.example: The hymn opens with the line about a wretch saved by grace.
senses.exampleCN: 这首赞美诗以一句「一个蒙恩得救的可怜人」开篇。
senses.why: In religious writing the exile became every struggling soul, which is why the word survives so strongly in hymns.
senses.whyCN: 在宗教书写里，流放者变成了每一个挣扎的灵魂，因此这个词在赞美诗中保存得特别牢固。

intro.en: Wretch comes from Old English wrecca, an exile or outcast, and its deeper Germanic source is generally reconstructed but not certain.
intro.cn: wretch 源自古英语 wrecca（流放者、被逐出者），更早的日耳曼语来源属于一般认为的重构形式，仍有争议。

items.en: A reconstructed noun of an exile is thought to lie behind the word; the exact form is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为这个词背后有一个表示「流放者」的重构名词，确切形式不确定。

items.en: Wrecca names a banished man, often one driven away for a crime.
items.cn: wrecca 指被放逐的人，常是因罪被赶出去的人。

items.en: The related verb wrecan means to drive out or avenge.
items.cn: 相关的动词 wrecan 意为驱逐或复仇。

items.en: Wrecca becomes wretch and is used for any unfortunate person.
items.cn: wrecca 演变为 wretch，开始用来指任何不幸的人。

items.en: The word enters hymns and literary writing as a name for a sinful or pitiable person.
items.cn: 这个词进入赞美诗和文学写作，用来称呼有罪或可怜的人。

items.en: Modern English keeps both the pitying and the contemptuous uses.
items.cn: 现代英语同时保留了怜惜与轻蔑两种用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words beginning with the same w-r cluster; the near-meaning group gathers other words for unfortunates and for despicable men.
note.cn: 形近组收开头字母相同的一组词；近义组收其他表示不幸者与卑鄙之徒的词。

entries.definition: Miserable, unfortunate, or of very poor quality; the adjective built from wretch.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，由 wretch 派生，义为「悲惨的、不幸的、糟透的」。

entries.definition: To make the sound and movement of vomiting; it merely loses the w and comes from a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「干呕」；只是少了一个 w 的拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The joint between the hand and the arm; it begins with the same silent w but is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「手腕」；开头同样是不发音的 w，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Very unhappy or uncomfortable; this is the adjective usually used when pity is wanted.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「悲惨的、痛苦的」，是表达怜惜时最常用的词。

entries.definition: A person rejected by society; the closest modern equivalent of the oldest sense of wretch.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「被社会抛弃的人」，是 wretch 最古老义项最接近的现代说法。

entries.definition: A wicked or dishonest person; a stronger and more literary insult than the contemptuous wretch.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「恶棍、无赖」，作为骂人的话比表示轻蔑的 wretch 更重、更书面。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English root and the fixed phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子基于真实的古英语词根，以及这个词固定出现的搭配。

normal.en: Wrecca meant an exile, so every wretch is someone pushed out of home.
normal.cn: wrecca 指流放者，所以每个 wretch 都是被推出家门的人。

normal.en: Add -ed and you get wretched, the adjective for miserable things and lives.
normal.cn: 加上 -ed 就成了 wretched，用来形容悲惨的事物与生活。

normal.en: Poor wretch is pity; you wretch is contempt; the phrase decides the tone.
normal.cn: poor wretch 表示怜惜，you wretch 表示轻蔑，前面的词决定语气。

normal.en: The plural is wretches with -es after the ch sound.
normal.cn: 复数写作 wretches，因为 ch 音后要加 -es。

normal.en: Compare retch: retch loses the w and means to gag, so the w marks the person, not the sickness.
normal.cn: 对比 retch：retch 少了 w，表示干呕，所以 w 标记的是人，不是病痛。

abstract.en: Picture a ragged figure hunched in the rain while others hurry past.
abstract.cn: 想象一个衣衫破烂的人蜷在雨里，别人匆匆走过。

abstract.en: Picture the same figure spitting insults back, and the pity turns to contempt.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个人反过来口出恶言，怜惜就变成了轻蔑。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny child under one blanket with a torch and a book.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小孩子，裹着一条毯子，举着手电看书。

examples.en: She found a wretch asleep in the doorway and brought him a blanket.
examples.cn: 她发现一个流浪汉睡在门口，给他拿来一条毯子。

examples.en: The ungrateful wretch never even said thank you.
examples.cn: 那个忘恩负义的家伙连句谢谢都没说。

examples.en: The old song calls the singer a wretch who needs saving.
examples.cn: 那首老歌把歌者称作一个需要被拯救的可怜人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「惹扯」——被人一「惹」就「扯」进争执，结果被赶出门外，成了可怜人；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 wrecca「流放者、被逐出的人」→ 中古英语 wretch「不幸的人」→ 现代英语 wretch（可怜人；卑鄙之徒）。同源动词 wrecan 意为驱逐、复仇。更早的日耳曼语形式为重构形式，来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Wretch moves from the exile to the unfortunate, then flips to the despised and the humble, and finally settles in song and story.
sensesIntro.cn: wretch 从流放者走向不幸的人，再翻转为被鄙视者与卑微者，最后落脚在歌曲与故事里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ragged figure hunched in the rain, pushed out and left behind.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个衣衫破烂的人蜷在雨里，被推出门外、留在原地。

branches.en: The exile who suffers is both the oldest sense and the everyday one of pity.
branches.cn: 受苦的流放者既是最古老的义项，也是日常表达怜惜的义项。

branches.en: The same exile who deserves contempt turns the word into an insult.
branches.cn: 同一个流放者一旦被认为活该，这个词就变成了骂人的话。

branches.en: Children and animals who seem helpless extend the word into gentle pity.
branches.cn: 看着无助的孩子和动物把词义延伸到温和的怜悯。

branches.en: The person slips away and the misery itself is left in the noun.
branches.cn: 人退出了画面，只剩苦难本身留在这个名词里。

branches.en: Pity made into song keeps the figure alive in hymns and stories.
branches.cn: 把怜悯写进歌里，让这个形象在赞美诗和故事中延续。

intro.en: Wretch is a short native noun; its family grows with -ed and -ness, while the -ch ending is part of the base spelling.
intro.cn: wretch 是英语本族语的短名词，它的同族词靠 -ed 与 -ness 扩展，结尾的 -ch 属于词干拼写的一部分。

latinIntro.en: Wretch has no Latin ancestor; the Latin entries below are words of the same exile and outcast field.
latinIntro.cn: wretch 没有拉丁语祖先；下面的拉丁同族词属于同一「流放、被逐」义场的词。

items.example: Wrecca is the direct ancestor of wretch.
items.exampleCN: wrecca 是 wretch 的直接祖先。

items.example: Wrecan shows the driving-out sense behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: wrecan 显示出这个名词背后的「赶出去」义。

items.meaning: forming an adjective with the given character
items.meaningCN: 构成形容词的词尾，表示具有某种特征
items.example: The suffix -ed forms wretched from wretch.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 由 wretch 构成 wretched。

items.meaning: forming an abstract noun of state
items.meaningCN: 构成表示状态抽象名词的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ness forms wretchedness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 wretchedness。

items.example: The plural takes -es after the ch sound.
items.exampleCN: 复数在 ch 音后加 -es。

items.meaning: the plural ending used after ch
items.meaningCN: 在 ch 音后构成复数的词尾
items.example: The plural ending -es adds a syllable to the noun.
items.exampleCN: 复数词尾 -es 给名词增加一个音节。

items.meaning: full of misery, an archaic form
items.meaningCN: 充满悲惨的，属古旧形式
items.example: Wretchful existed alongside wretched in older English.
items.exampleCN: 在更早的英语中 wretchful 与 wretched 并存。

items.example: Poor in front of the noun gives the pitying tone.
items.exampleCN: 名词前的 poor 赋予怜惜语气。

definition_zh: 皱纹；褶皱；皱起；起皱；好主意；妙计；技巧
definition_en: a small line or fold on a surface, especially the skin, or to make such a line appear
core_image: 一块布被轻轻捏起，表面凸出一道细细的褶子
scene: 阳光斜照进窗户，老人摊开报纸，眉眼间也有浅浅的纹路。He gave me a wide smile full of wrinkles around the eyes.
sceneCN: 这里 wrinkle 是「皱纹」（第 1 个义项：皮肤上细小的褶痕）；句意为他的脸舒展开来，露出满是细细褶痕的微笑。

collocations.zh: 皱起鼻子（表示气味难闻或厌恶）
皱起眉头（表示思考或不悦）

derivatives.zh: 由 wrinkle 加 -ed 构成，义为「有皱纹的、起皱的」
由 wrinkle 加 -y 构成，义为「多皱纹的、皮皱皱的」
由 wrinkle 加 -ing 构成，义为「起皱的过程、皱褶」
由前缀 anti-「抗、防」+ wrinkle 构成，义为「抗皱的」

senses.title: A line on the skin
senses.definition: a small line or fold on the skin, especially one caused by age or by frowning
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤上细小的纹路或褶痕，尤因年长或皱眉而形成
senses.example: She laughed and a fan of wrinkles spread from the corner of each eye.
senses.exampleCN: 她笑了，眼角散开一片皱纹。
senses.why: Old English gewrinclod already meant to wind or twist, and a fold of skin is the twist seen from outside.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 gewrinclod 已经表示「缠绕、扭曲」，皮肤的褶子就是从外面看到的那一扭。

senses.title: A fold on a surface
senses.definition: a small fold or crease in cloth, paper, or another material
senses.definitionCN: 布料、纸张或其他材料上细小的折痕
senses.example: Iron the shirt well, or it will show a wrinkle by morning.
senses.exampleCN: 把衬衫熨好，不然到明天早上就会出褶子。
senses.why: The same twisting action shows up on any flat surface, so the word moves easily from skin to cloth and paper.
senses.whyCN: 同样的扭曲作用出现在任何平面上，所以这个词可以轻松从皮肤转到布和纸上。

senses.title: To contract into folds
senses.definition: to make part of the face or a surface pull together into small folds
senses.definitionCN: 使面部某处或某个表面挤在一起形成细褶
senses.example: The baby wrinkled her nose at the smell of the medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 宝宝闻到药味皱起了鼻子。
senses.why: The noun becomes a verb once the action of pulling skin together is named by the same form.
senses.whyCN: 当「把皮肤挤到一起」这个动作也由同一个形式来命名时，名词就转成了动词。

senses.title: A small problem or doubt
senses.definition: a small problem or doubt that has to be smoothed out
senses.definitionCN: 需要被抹平的小问题或疑虑
senses.example: There is one wrinkle in the plan that we must deal with.
senses.exampleCN: 计划里还有一处小麻烦需要我们处理。
senses.why: A crease in a cloth means the cloth is not yet flat, so a wrinkle in a plan means the plan is not yet smooth.
senses.whyCN: 布上的褶意味着布还没铺平，所以计划里的皱褶就表示计划还不够顺。

senses.title: A clever new trick
senses.definition: a clever new method, idea, or detail added to something
senses.definitionCN: 新加进某事的聪明方法、主意或巧思
senses.example: The app adds a new wrinkle to the old idea of a travel diary.
senses.exampleCN: 这个应用给旅行日记这个老点子添了新花样。
senses.why: In American use the new fold in a smooth pattern became a clever modification, and from there a fresh trick.
senses.whyCN: 美式用法把平整图案上新添的褶说成一种聪明的改动，由此又引申为新奇的手法。

senses.title: To be able to smooth out
senses.definition: to develop or show small folds, used of materials, often in the negative
senses.definitionCN: 材料自身出现或显出细褶，常用于否定说法
senses.example: This cotton jacket will not wrinkle even after a long flight.
senses.exampleCN: 这件棉外套即使长途飞行之后也不会起皱。
senses.why: When the subject is the cloth itself, the verb describes a property of the material rather than an action on it.
senses.whyCN: 当主语是布料本身时，这个动词描述的便是材料自身的性质，而不是对它施加的动作。

intro.en: Wrinkle probably goes back to an Old English adjective gewrinclod, to wind or twist, and a related noun wrincle; the deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: wrinkle 一般认为可追溯到古英语形容词 gewrinclod（缠绕、扭曲）及相关名词 wrincle；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: A reconstructed root meaning to turn or twist is thought to lie behind the word.
items.cn: 一般认为这个词背后有一个表示「转动、扭曲」的重构词根。

items.en: The adjective gewrinclod means full of turnings or twists.
items.cn: 形容词 gewrinclod 意为满是弯折、扭曲的。

items.en: The noun wrincle, a fold or crease, appears beside it.
items.cn: 与之并列出现的是名词 wrincle，指褶子、折痕。

items.en: Wrincle becomes wrinkle and is used of skin and cloth alike.
items.cn: wrincle 演变为 wrinkle，皮肤和布料都可以用。

items.en: The verb is established, and the extra-idea sense appears in American use.
items.cn: 动词用法确立，美国用法中又出现了「新点子」这一义项。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the same silent w or a similar -nkle tail; the near-meaning group gathers other words for folds, lines and small tricks.
note.cn: 形近组收同样以不发音 w 开头、或结尾相近的词；近义组收其他表示褶子、纹路与小把戏的词。

entries.definition: Having small lines or folds; the adjective made directly from the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，由这个动词直接构成，义为「有皱纹的、起皱的」。

entries.definition: To scatter drops or grains over something; it merely shares the -inkle ending and comes from another root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「撒、洒」；只是结尾 -inkle 相近，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A small edible sea snail, also a British verb meaning to dig out; unrelated in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「峨螺」，英式英语中也作动词表示「掏出」；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A line made in cloth or paper by folding and pressing; sharper than a soft wrinkle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「折痕、压出褶」，由折叠压平形成，比柔软的皱纹更锐利。

entries.definition: A deep line in the skin or ground; deeper and longer than a wrinkle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「沟、深纹」，多用于额头或土地，比 wrinkle 更深更长。

entries.definition: To form small crisp folds, as paper or leaves do; often lighter and cruder than a wrinkle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「起皱、皱褶」，多指纸或叶子那种又轻又脆的褶。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English root, the word family, and the phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子基于真实的古英语词根、同族词，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: The silent w hides in wrinkle, wring and wreath; only the r is heard.
normal.cn: 不发音的 w 藏在 wrinkle、wring、wreath 里，耳朵只听到 r 的音。

normal.en: The adjective wrinkled works for cloth and for faces alike.
normal.cn: wrinkled 这个形容词对布料和面孔同样适用。

normal.en: Wrinkle your nose shows distaste, and wrinkle your brow shows doubt.
normal.cn: wrinkle your nose 表示嫌弃，wrinkle your brow 表示怀疑。

normal.en: A new wrinkle in American speech means a clever extra trick, not a fold in the skin.
normal.cn: 美式口语里的 new wrinkle 指巧妙的额外花样，而不是皮肤上的褶子。

normal.en: Anti-wrinkle cream uses the Greek prefix anti-, meaning against.
normal.cn: anti-wrinkle cream 用的是希腊语前缀 anti-，意为「反对、防」。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pinching a thin cloth, and one fine line rising under the fingers.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手捏起薄布，指尖下凸起一道细纹。

abstract.en: Picture a laughing face, with lines spreading out like a folded fan.
abstract.cn: 想象一张笑开的脸，纹路像折扇一样铺开。

abstract.en: Picture a map with one small fold left in it, so the route never lies fully flat.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图上留着一道小折痕，路线始终铺不平。

examples.en: Deep wrinkles around his eyes showed how often he had laughed.
examples.cn: 他眼边的深皱纹说明他常常大笑。

examples.en: The new teacher wrinkled her forehead at the noise in the hall.
examples.cn: 新来的老师听到走廊里的吵闹声皱起了眉头。

examples.en: The team added a clever wrinkle to the old rule: everyone must share one idea.
examples.cn: 团队给这条老规矩加了一个巧妙的新花样：人人都要贡献一个想法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「润扣」——衣领处有一道没「润」平的褶，扣子一扣就鼓起一条线；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 一般认为源自古英语形容词 gewrinclod「缠绕、扭曲的」及相关名词 wrincle「褶子、折痕」，核心义是「扭起来形成的细褶」；更早的日耳曼语词根为重构形式，来源不确定。
